 Keli Zinn releases statement explaining decision to keep head football coach Greg Schiano
 Rutgers athletic director Keli Zinn has released a statement that explains her decision to keep head coach Greg Schiano for the 2027 season
 Bobby Deren 53 Rutgers athletic director Keli Zinn has released a statement that explains her decision to keep head coach Greg Schiano for the 2027 season. The statement comes as Rutgers is preparing to play Nebraska following a 31-10 loss to Wisconsin that officially knocked the Scarlet Knights out of bowl contention.
 Here is a full look at the statement.
 "Our 2026 football season has fallen well below our expectations and has understandably led to frustration from our passionate fans and supporters. As your Director of Athletics and as a competitor at heart, I feel those same emotions. Our results are not acceptable for the expectations we have for our football program and for the athletics program we are building.
 However, I also have an obligation to make decisions that serve the best long-term interests of Rutgers University. There are several factors that go into decisions regarding the hiring and retention of head coaches in all of our sports, especially football and basketball. After weighing all factors, and consulting with University leadership, Head Coach Greg Schiano will be returning in 2027. Let me be very clear: this decision is not reflective of a lowering of standards or an indication that everything is fine. It is not.
 This is instead a reflection of my belief that we have an opportunity to make meaningful changes that will strengthen our roster and better position our program to compete and win at a higher level. Coach and I have met repeatedly to discuss the future and I am encouraged by the plan he has developed, and we have a clear understanding of what can best position us for success next season. While we both recognize that plans alone do not produce wins, we share in a belief that necessary changes will help deliver the competitive results we all expect for our football program. 
 I believe deeply in what is possible at Rutgers. I remain committed to building an athletics department that our student-athletes, coaches, university, donors, corporate partners, alumni, and fans can be proud of. That includes our football program. I know our fans are tired of hearing about what Rutgers Football can become. You want to see results and it's our responsibility to make sure we deliver."
 The last time Zinn spoke publicly about S-chiano was hours before the start of the season when Rutgers lost to UMass by a final score of 37-21. 
 "You're not going to see me, get in the habit of speaking public about specific expectations when you get into wins and losses," Zinn said on Sept 3 . "I don't love that, right? And instead, Greg and I are on the exact same page with this. I want what he wants, and he wants what I want. And what that is in its simplest form is to improve what we saw from last year."
 Rutgers finished 5-7 in 2025.
